use_case.name: Manufacturing Knowledge Assistant
use_case.description: Role-aware assistant that answers employee questions from internal policies, equipment manuals, and management documents with citations, enforcing role-based access control so restricted documents are never retrieved or disclosed to unauthorized employees.

business_spec.current_process: Employees manually search across internal policies, equipment manuals, and management documents to find answers to their questions, with no systematic way to verify which source supports an answer.
pain_points: Manual search across the document collection is slow
Answers can be incomplete or unsupported because employees may overlook the applicable source
business_spec.proposed_solution: An AI assistant that answers employee questions using the document collection, provides citations to the supporting source, and enforces role-based access so restricted documents are never retrieved or disclosed to unauthorized employees.
stakeholders: knowledge owners (maintain and classify the source documents)
target_outputs: role-aware answer to an employee question, grounded with citations to the supporting source
business_spec.success_criteria: Employees find reliable answers faster, can verify answers through citations, and never receive content outside their role. No numerical time-saving, accuracy, cost, or adoption target was specified.
expected_value: faster access to reliable internal knowledge
enforced access boundaries that prevent unauthorized disclosure
risks: retrieval of restricted chunks into the model context
leakage of restricted content through answer text or citations
returning an answer when the authorized collection contains no support
business_spec.poc_goal: Demonstrate role-aware, citation-grounded question answering over three sample PDFs (employee travel policy, MX-200 maintenance manual, Project Aurora pricing strategy) using a supplied access manifest and query set. Run `python run_poc.py --input <path-to-poc_input_bundle.json>`, resolve the other supplied files relative to that bundle, execute the four role-tagged queries, and save non-empty parseable JSON results demonstrating correct access decisions and citations. Out of scope for this first PoC: a web interface, a live document-repository connector, enterprise sign-in/identity integration, a full audit-log service, and a numerical RAG-quality threshold.

input_formats: json (access manifest, query set, input bundle)
technical_spec.domain_vocabulary: No controlled term list required. Exact values and units must be preserved verbatim as they appear in the source documents (e.g. EUR amounts, operating hours, bar pressure, percentages).
technical_spec.data_sources: PoC uses a local fixture bundle: three sample PDFs (employee_travel_policy.pdf, mx200_maintenance_manual.pdf, project_aurora_pricing_strategy.pdf) plus access_manifest.json and query_set.json, all resolved relative to poc_input_bundle.json. Connection to a live enterprise document repository is out of scope for this PoC.

model_preferences.embedding_model: Azure OpenAI embedding deployment supported by RAGWorkflow; exact deployment name is an environment setting

technical_spec.security_constraints: Role-based access filtering must occur before retrieval, so unauthorized chunks never enter the model's context window. The requesting role is trusted request metadata and must not be inferred from the question text. Denied answers must not reveal restricted facts or citations. External model APIs are allowed. The synthetic PoC fixtures contain no personal data. Enterprise identity integration and a full audit-log service are out of scope for the PoC (simulated role values, local vector store only). No exact data-retention period was specified.
technical_spec.evaluation_requirements: Deterministic acceptance test using the four supplied role-tagged queries (Q01-Q04), checked against required facts, the exact access decision (allowed/denied), and required citation pairs per query. No numerical RAG-quality threshold (e.g. a fixed recall/precision score) was specified for the first PoC.
technical_spec.runtime_interface: CLI: `python run_poc.py --input <path-to-poc_input_bundle.json>`, resolving access_manifest.json, query_set.json, and the documents directory relative to that bundle file.

field_descriptions.query_id: Identifier of the incoming query, preserved unchanged from the input.
field_descriptions.role: Requesting role, preserved unchanged from the input; trusted metadata, never inferred from the question.
field_descriptions.question: The employee's question, preserved unchanged from the input.
field_descriptions.access_decision: Whether the role was authorized to receive a factual answer to this question.
field_descriptions.answer: The grounded answer text, or a refusal message when denied or when the authorized sources do not support an answer.
field_descriptions.citations: Supporting citations as [file_name, page_number] pairs; empty when denied.
field_descriptions.refusal_reason: Explanation for a denied or not-found answer; null when access_decision is allowed and the answer is fully supported.

target_output_spec.missing_value_policy: If the authorized sources do not support an answer, state that the information was not found and do not speculate. If sources conflict, identify the conflict and cite both sources. Never fabricate a citation.
validation_rules: An allowed factual answer requires at least one citation to a document permitted for that role
A denied answer requires an empty citations list, a non-null refusal_reason, and must not reveal restricted facts
Each citation is a two-element list [file_name (str), page_number (1-based int)], in that order
query_id and role must be preserved unchanged from the input query
Cite every material factual claim using [file_name, page_number]
Do not answer from model memory when authorized evidence is absent

assumptions.text: No numerical success/adoption/time-saving target was specified; success is defined qualitatively (faster reliable answers, verifiable citations, no out-of-role disclosure).
The exact Azure OpenAI embedding deployment name was not specified; the PoC will read it from an environment variable and default to a model compatible with RAGWorkflow (text-embedding-3-large).
No exact data-retention period was specified for PoC outputs; recorded as not_specified.
No numerical RAG-quality threshold (e.g. recall/precision score) was specified; evaluation for the first PoC is the four-query deterministic acceptance test only.

Whether real production documents (beyond the synthetic PoC fixtures) contain personal data is unknown; this is recorded as 'unknown' in governance.data_handling and will block production packaging until confirmed.

Business-process participants were not specified; defaulted to a single 'Employee / Manager' requesting-user lane for the query-submission step, with no separate Knowledge Owner lane since document classification is treated as static input.
Document classification and allowed-role tagging (as in access_manifest.json) is treated as static input data, not a modeled manual business step performed by knowledge owners.
A denied query ends the process cleanly with a refusal; no escalation/appeal path to a knowledge owner was requested.

selected_modules.name: RAGWorkflow
selected_modules.reason: Document collection to cited answer -- RAGWorkflow covers indexing, retrieval, and cited-answer generation end-to-end, using a local persistent vector store (Chroma) and supports query-time metadata filters (ask(filters=...)) which are the mechanism used for pre-retrieval RBAC enforcement.

custom_components: RoleScopedIngestion -- attaches role_<role> boolean metadata flags to each chunk (derived from access_manifest.json allowed_roles) before embedding, using RAGWorkflow's own embedder/vector_store attributes instead of its index_documents() convenience wrapper (which has no metadata-injection hook)
AccessDecisionClassifier -- an internal-only unfiltered relevance check, never exposed as content, used solely to distinguish a restricted-topic denial from an honest not-found

steps.name: Provide document classification and allowed-roles manifest
Index documents with role metadata, retrieve role-filtered context, generate cited answer per query

parameters.access_control: Pre-retrieval RBAC: each indexed chunk is tagged with boolean role_<role> metadata flags derived from access_manifest.json's allowed_roles; ask() is called with filters={'role_<requesting_role>': true} so unauthorized chunks are excluded from the similarity search itself (Chroma 'where' clause / in-memory pre-filter), never entering the model context.
parameters.denial_classification: An additional internal-only unfiltered search (never exposed as content) checks whether the best-matching chunk for the query belongs to a role-restricted document; if so, and no strong authorized match exists, access_decision is 'denied' with a generic refusal_reason; if no strong match exists anywhere, the answer states the information was not found.

decision_points.name: Is the requesting role authorized for this content?

traceability.required_by: security_constraints: role-based access filtering must occur before retrieval

change_log.change: Initial blueprint generated by solution_configuration_wizard V1

PoC scaffolded and hand-wired: RAGWorkflow's own parser/embedder/vector-store/retriever driven directly (instead of index_documents()/ask()) to attach role_<role> metadata at ingestion and apply pre-retrieval filters at query time; answer generation calls the underlying chat client directly (not AnswerGenerator.generate(), which hardcodes temperature=0.0) to honor the user's explicit temperature=1.0 and reasoning_effort=medium; hand-authored schemas/output_schema.py (RAGAnswerRecord) since SchemaGenerator is not invoked for the rag pattern; replaced the generic scaffolded evals/run_basic_eval.py (which had a syntax error and did not model RBAC) with a deterministic 4-query acceptance check against evals/ground_truth/expected_results.json.
